Subject: Renewal negotiation — Q4 spike and short-term credits

Hey Evelyn,

Quick context: BlueNova's ingest and model usage will likely spike in Q4 due to a regulatory labeling effort. We’re close to signing an annual renewal but need a short-term operational guardrail to avoid outsized overage costs during the three-month ramp.

Can Redwood provide a temporary price-hold for overages (Oct–Dec), plus a one-time ramp credit applied to the first invoice post-renewal? We’re aiming to keep the committed base unchanged but need predictability on short-term unit economics.

If you can outline a simple structure (credit amount, eligibility, and how it interacts with true-ups), I’ll surface internally and share timing for signature.

Thanks — Daniel

Thanks Daniel — appreciate the signal. Quick read below on a pragmatic approach that keeps your committed baseline intact while smoothing the spike. Attached is a one-page workbook that models examples at +20/ +50/ +100% usage.

Proposal (short version):
- Temporary overage price-hold (Oct 1–Dec 31): cap overage unit price at current committed rate + 10% (instead of the standard retail overage price). Caps apply only to usage above the contracted commit.
- One-time ramp credit: $60k applied to the first invoice after renewal signature. Credit applies only if usage in Oct–Dec exceeds 110% of the committed monthly average.
- True-up treatment: standard true-up applies at term end; credits reduce the next invoice but do not change committed volumes.
- Eligibility: must sign renewal and new PO by Sep 15.

Operational notes:
- We’ll document credit and price-hold as an amendment (two-clause addendum). Finance must approve for revenue recognition; copying Marissa and Ben to confirm.
- If you want automatic telemetry alerts (traffic thresholds) to avoid surprises, we can enable threshold notifications in the Console.

If that reads OK, Ben and I will draft the amendment and a short SOW for internal approvals.

Cheers,
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
